cells.tense: You're in the fog with your eyes open, and you're not waiting for it to lift before you move.
cells.ask: offer the next step to the fire you'd actually keep lit — the one person or project you'd tend all your life if it asked nothing back — and give it one honest hour today.
cells.core:
You have enough to go on, and you're not pretending otherwise. Not the whole road — just the next step, which is all anyone gets. You feel your way forward and the feeling turns out to be information, and nothing in you is fighting that. The fog isn't a problem you're solving. It's the condition you're walking in, and you're walking well.

Keep the fire you've found. Pick the thing you'd still be tending if it never thanked you, and give it an hour today — not because it's owed, but because steady tending is what turns a hunch into a life.
cells.sheetLine: You're moving through the fog without needing it to clear first.
cells.place: in the fog, taking the next step on light you don't have yet

cells.tense: You're already living past the fog, bracing for a road that hasn't been drawn yet.
cells.ask: water one small thing you're actually growing and leave it alone for a week — let it come up at its own speed instead of willing it up faster.
cells.core:
When this is working, you read a room before anyone speaks and you trust what you find. You move through uncertainty at an easy pace, one step at a time, and the steps keep arriving. That's the hand you're playing with — a feel for what's coming that most people don't have.

Right now it's running ahead of you. You can feel what's coming before it comes, and it's stopped being a gift. Every version of what might happen gets lived in advance, and the future gets carried around like something already decided. The sensitivity is real. It's just aimed past today, and today is the only place the next step can be taken from. Slow the reach down. Tend one small thing that's actually here — a person, a patch of work, a habit — and give it a week of care without checking whether it's growing.

cells.tense: You stopped mid-step a while back, and you're still standing where you stopped.
cells.ask: listen to one thing with nothing to gain from it — no fixing, no deciding — and let it be exactly what it is before you respond.
cells.core:
When this is working, the fog doesn't stop you — you take the next step on the light you have and let the rest of the road stay dark until you reach it. That's a live skill, and it was yours. You walked into conditions you couldn't see the end of and found your footing as you went.

The fog is still there. You're not walking into it. Somewhere back along the way, the next step got expensive — so the reaching stopped, and the not-knowing turned into a place to stand still rather than a place to move from. The capacity hasn't gone anywhere. It's just not being used. Don't try to manufacture wonder or force the feeling back. Practice listening instead — small, honest, first-impression listening, where the point is to perceive and not to decide. That pulls the current back through, and the next step gets visible again.
cells.sheetLine: You've stopped stepping into the fog and you're standing at the edge.

cells.tense: You're already navigating this, and you're telling yourself it's just how things are.
cells.ask: pick one hunch you've been treating as a mood and run it like a skill — look at it, name why it fits, and act on it once on purpose.
cells.core:
This is a capacity you already have, and on a good day you'd recognize it: you sense what's underneath a situation and steer by it, and the steering holds up more often than not. You've done it in rooms where nobody else caught the shift.

And you call it a hunch, a mood, or just being careful. The guidance is running. The accounting for it isn't. You're already the one steering, and you describe it as though the situation were steering you. Give it a practice, so it stops looking like luck. Take one intuitive read and check it like a craft: say what you noticed, say why it fits what you know, act once on purpose. What is yours becomes visible when it's done deliberately.
